description: An embedded chief run inside a container or a Cuneiform Riju workspace must behave the same as a host run — but the engine makes assumptions that can break in a container: the `~/.chief` prefix (HOME may be unset, minimal, or read-only), worktree creation under `~/.chief/worktrees`, git identity, git 'dubious ownership' on a bind-mounted repo owned by another uid, and the reap/run-registry keys inside a foreign PID namespace. This tasklist makes those assumptions hold — or degrade cleanly — inside a container, so an embedding host can run `chief` in a per-language Riju container and get identical implement→verify→merge behavior. Builds on 80's headless contract. Scope: `engine/driver.sh` + `engine/lib.sh` (prefix/worktree/git resolution), `engine/reap.sh` (registry-key degradation), `docs/`.

userStories.title: Container-safe state prefix and worktrees
userStories.description: The state prefix and worktree root must resolve inside a container where HOME is unset/minimal/read-only or the repo is bind-mounted.
acceptanceCriteria: The state prefix (`CHIEF_PREFIX`/`CHIEF_RUNS`, default `~/.chief`) resolves correctly when HOME is unset or minimal — it is configurable via env with a documented container default, and a missing HOME does not crash the run
Worktree creation (default `~/.chief/worktrees/…`) works against a bind-mounted / container repo and is relocatable via env, so the worktree isolation the driver relies on holds inside a container

userStories.title: git assumptions hold under container ownership/identity
userStories.description: git must not refuse or prompt when the repo is owned by a different uid and no interactive identity exists.
acceptanceCriteria: git operations succeed for a repo owned by a uid different from the container user — the 'detected dubious ownership' case is handled or documented (e.g. a supported `safe.directory` setup)
A run does not require an interactive git identity: a default committer identity is available or documented for the container case, so commits/merges do not fail for want of `user.name`/`user.email`

The reap/run-registry keys (cwd / argv `--chief-run=` / inherited `CHIEF_RUN_ID`) still function inside a container's PID namespace, or degrade to nothing rather than mis-reaping — consistent with `engine/reap.sh`'s existing degradation model

userStories.title: Document container/Riju operation and test the shaped conditions
userStories.description: Document what an embedding host must set, and test the container-shaped conditions that need no real container.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/` gains a "Running chief in a container / Riju workspace" section: the env to set (state prefix, worktree root, git `safe.directory`, committer identity), the guarantees, and what degrades

A hermetic test exercises the container-shaped conditions without a real container: HOME unset → prefix resolves via env; a run against a repo dir with the container-config env; the registry keys degrade cleanly rather than erroring or mis-matching
